title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 2 vs. Seattle Seahawks
headline: Cardinals' offense collapsed after halftime in a loss to Seattle; Marvin Harrison Jr. saw just two targets and Max Melton (foot) and Will Johnson (neck) left injured but aren't thought to be serious.
summary: LaFleur called the loss a weird, tough one and said the second half was self-inflicted. The offense went three-and-out and six-and-out repeatedly, after a first half that was tied 7-7 with good control of the game and time of possession. He said Arizona struggled on third down and blamed execution and detail errors, which he put on coaching and the need for better clarity. He said the passing game struggled when Jacoby Brissett was pressured, crediting Seattle's defensive coordinator for varying four-man rushes and pressure looks. He praised the defense for playing well until Seattle's long final drive of roughly 16 plays and 15 rushes, though he said the scheme wasn't good enough given the yardage allowed. He said he isn't concerned about Marvin Harrison Jr.'s two targets, explaining that heavy 13-personnel put only one receiver on the field and that the whole passing game was poor. He said Seattle's receiver, apparently Jaxon Smith-Njigba, is a dang good receiver and that the defense needs to limit his splash plays. Max Melton (foot) and Will Johnson (neck) both exited; LaFleur doesn't think either is serious but will update tomorrow, and he warned that adrenaline can mask pain. He said the team can't let the Seattle loss carry into next week against a good, healthy opponent.

injuries.detail: Exited with a foot injury; LaFleur doesn't think it's serious but will have more info tomorrow.
Exited with a neck injury; LaFleur doesn't think it's serious but will know more tomorrow.

signals.claim: Harrison's low target and snap count reflected heavy 13-personnel packages and a poor passing game, not a role change.
signals.note: He had only two targets and played about a third of the snaps, but LaFleur says he isn't concerned, so expect a bounce-back if the personnel mix changes.

signals.claim: The passing game struggled whenever Brissett was pressured by Seattle's varied rush looks.
signals.note: Pass-protection issues and a stalled offense cap Arizona's passing-game upside until they are fixed.
signals.quote: whether they're bringing the pressure bringing four man

signals.note: A defensive back's availability for next week is uncertain pending the update.
signals.quote: Max has a as a foot and then Will has a neck.

signals.claim: Johnson left the game with a neck injury and will be evaluated tomorrow.
signals.note: A defensive back's availability for next week is uncertain pending the update.
signals.quote: Max has a as a foot and then Will has a neck.

topics.detail: The offense went three-and-out and six-and-out in the second half and was poor on third down in the first half. LaFleur put the blame on coaching, clarity and play design, but said no panic button is being hit.

The defense played well until the last 20 minutes, then Seattle ran over 10 minutes with 16 plays and 15 rushes on its final drive. LaFleur said the scheme wasn't good enough and he still needs to review the tape on coverage against Seattle's top receiver.
Arizona used a lot of 13 personnel (one WR) in 'Z' and 'X' variations, which explains Harrison's lower snap share.

title: Kevin Stefanski reflects on Atlanta Falcons vs Carolina Panthers matchup | Press Conference
headline: Falcons got blown out by Carolina on turnovers. Penix is still progressing with no Week 3 plan, Rush is the current QB, and Terrell, Dorlus, Taylor and Ebukam are all in injury limbo before Thursday night.
summary: Stefanski was openly disappointed after a loss in which Atlanta fell into an early hole, never recovered, and lost the turnover battle badly. They gave the ball away repeatedly, including on the first play, and forced no takeaways. He listed four injuries (a hamstring, a groin, a thumb and a rib) and said more information would come after testing. On quarterback play, he praised Cooper Rush's effort but would not assess Rush or Jack Strand individually, saying the failure was the whole team's and he didn't want to single out one position. He gave no Penix update beyond saying Penix keeps progressing, and he would not say whether Penix could play on the short week. He also declined to say who starts in Week 3 if neither Penix nor Tua Tagovailoa is available. He wouldn't comment on whether Rush's back was bothering him or affected his play. He took responsibility for the failed fourth-and-one end-around to Drake London, crediting the defense with making the play. He blamed the lack of red-zone trips through two games on turnovers and turnovers on downs.

injuries.detail: Groin injury suffered in the game; awaiting testing and more information.
Dealt with a thumb injury; awaiting testing.
Rib injury; awaiting testing.
Hamstring injury (name garbled in captions as 'Sam Sampson', likely Ebukam); awaiting testing.

topics.detail: Stefanski said the game was decided by giveaways and takeaways: Atlanta turned it over many times, including on the first play, and forced none. He called the mistakes correctable.
He took responsibility for the end-around call to Drake London on fourth-and-one. He said a blocking assignment was supposed to be accounted for, but he credited the defender for making the play.
Atlanta has had no red-zone trips in the first two games, which Stefanski attributed to turnovers and a turnover on downs ending drives.
The team turns quickly to a Thursday night game. Stefanski declined to say who would start Week 3 if neither Penix nor Tua Tagovailoa is available.
He said the team has resolve and resilience despite visible sideline frustration and boos. He said he doesn't react to the crowd and that the team needs to give fans reason to support it.

title: Dave Canales evaluates Week 2 win over Falcons
headline: Panthers rolled 34-3 behind a dominant Devin Lloyd; Jonathon Brooks re-aggravated his groin (day-to-day), while Darren Waller and Xavier Legette had big roles.
summary: Dave Canales called the 34-3 win over Atlanta complementary football. The defense forced four turnovers plus a couple of fourth-down stops, which gave the offense short fields, though the offense missed chances in the red zone. He said penalties wiped out roughly 60-70 rushing yards and need cleaning up, starting with stance and footwork. Devin Lloyd was the star: two interceptions (one returned for a touchdown), a sack, eight tackles and a batted pass, which Canales called one of the best linebacker games he has seen. Xavier Legette made the big late play that Canales called the momentum tipping point, after his best week of practice, and Bryce Young then threw a touchdown to Darren Waller. Canales praised Young's ownership of the offense, including tweaking routes with receivers and trusting anticipatory throws and play-action shots to Jalen Coker. Waller was described as exactly the matchup weapon against safeties and linebackers the team signed him to be. On injuries, Jonathon Brooks re-aggravated a groin issue and is day-to-day, and a player named Nick (rib/abdominal) and a player Canales called Claude Cherilus (shoulder) are being evaluated.

injuries.detail: Re-aggravated his groin when he bounced a run to the left toward the sideline and it got sore; day-to-day, with more information expected as the week goes on.
Rib/abdominal injury; the team will keep evaluating to see if they can get him turned around quickly.
Shoulder injury that kept him from finishing the game.
Evaluated for a concussion but was fine; he was cramping and sat back down.
Was fine and came back into the game.

signals.note: A huge IDP performance (2 INTs, 1 TD, a sack, 8 tackles) that Canales credited to his preparation and being in the right spots.
signals.quote: one of the most dominant linebacker performances I've seen

signals.claim: Legette will keep getting deep-ball opportunities after hitting multiple 40+ yard connections with Young in practice.
signals.note: Canales called his late big play the game's tipping point and said he had his best practice week yet, which supports more downfield looks.
signals.quote: Xavier had the best week he's had of practice

signals.note: He scored twice, per the coach's mention of his second touchdown, and has built timing with Young that makes him a red-zone target.
signals.quote: Just the ability to take advantage of matchups with safeties, with linebackers.

signals.claim: Young will keep fine-tuning routes with receivers and trusting anticipatory and play-action throws downfield.
signals.note: Canales framed the offense as Young's, with growing trust and timing with his pass catchers, which is a good sign for the passing game.
signals.quote: watching this offense become Bryce's offense

signals.note: A re-aggravated groin puts his availability and workload in doubt for next week's game.

signals.claim: Coker is a punt-return option, and his returns helped flip field position.
signals.note: Extra special-teams touches add some upside; Canales also cited play-action shots to Coker in the offense.
signals.quote: Jalen Coker with an amazing first punt return.

topics.detail: Canales estimated penalties cost the offense about 60-70 rushing yards. He said the fix starts with stance and keeping feet running to keep hands clean.
The team's first-drive fourth-down try was a comfort-zone decision, not a tone-setter. Canales said they go for it regularly and Young is comfortable in those spots.
The defense expected Atlanta to run after last week and responded by playing assignments, setting edges and tackling well in the secondary. Canales praised the young defensive group that stepped in.
Canales said the coverage units were fast and physical and the return game produced yardage that led to points. McMillan also volunteered to return punts, so there are options.
The offense left points on the field in the red zone despite the short fields the defense provided.

title: Zac Taylor Recaps Week 2 Victory Over Texans | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Bengals beat the Texans 20-6 on defense and special teams. Zac Taylor shrugged off Ja'Marr Chase's target volume, said Joe Burrow's injury was no concern, and praised Drew Sample's blocking.
summary: Taylor opened by crediting the defense for setting the tone on the road. He pointed to the early field position it created, the sack production, and Dexter Lawrence's fourth-and-one stop, which he said may have affected two plays. He also praised the punt team for pinning Houston deep, and said the offense should have scored more off those short fields. He called the day hard-fought against a Texans front he considers elite, with gritty yards in the run game and a lot of pressure on the offense. Asked about Ja'Marr Chase's usage, Taylor dismissed it as an easy talking point, said Chase was a captain who stayed positive, and said production will come. He said Joe Burrow's legs came back in game two, that he took sacks but found soft spots and made explosive plays, and that his injury did not concern him based on Burrow's feedback during the week. He gave Drew Sample high praise for his blocking, leadership and protection work, saying the stat sheet will never show his value. He also said the aggressive play-calling was dialed down in the second half because of the lead and the Houston pass rush, and that the offense still has things to clean up.

injuries.detail: Played through whatever he was dealing with. Taylor said the injury didn't concern him based on Burrow's feedback over the last couple of days, and he called everything the way he wanted.

signals.claim: Chase's production and targets will come in this offense in the coming weeks, even if the volume was low this week.
signals.note: Taylor waved off concern about Chase's target share and said the volume tends to even out, so this is a hold or buy-low-leaning situation.
signals.quote: He knew this stuff's going to come.

signals.claim: Burrow is healthy enough for the full playbook and is not a concern going forward.
signals.note: The coach is not worried about Burrow's health. Sacks and hits against pass-rush-heavy fronts are the risk to watch.
signals.quote: the injury didn't concern me based on the feedback he'd given me

signals.claim: Sample will keep a key role as a blocker in the run game and protection, including chipping and playing running back in protection.
signals.note: His value is blocking and leadership, not receiving production, so he has little fantasy upside.
signals.quote: he's not going to get a lot of love for all that

signals.note: Lawrence made a key fourth-and-one stop and was a disruptive force on the defensive line, which helps for IDP leagues.
signals.quote: he may have impacted two plays right there

topics.detail: The defense set the tone with sack production, plays on the ball and a strong run defense. Taylor said stopping the run let the defense tee off on a Houston offense that had to lean on the run.
The punt team kept Houston deep, with seven possessions starting inside the 25. Taylor credited the unit for a big part of the win.

Taylor called the Texans' front, including Will Anderson, who moved around a lot, extremely tough. The Bengals ground out yards and ran the ball in tough situations. They dialed back aggression in the second half with the lead.
Burrow took hits and sacks, and Taylor said that is not what they want. He said Burrow got his legs back in game two and made some big conversions.
Taylor said the defense is coming together in year two with the same staff and the team has momentum. He said the offense still has things to clean up.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference at Buccaneers: September 20th, 2026
headline: Browns beat Tampa Bay 23-19 after a long weather delay; Deshaun Watson praised for a strong second half, but Monken dodged the question of whether he starts vs. Carolina and admitted the run game needs fixing.
summary: Monken was proud of the team for battling back after an ugly first half and winning 23-19 at Tampa Bay, following a rough Week 1. He said the team used the lengthy delay to hydrate, fuel up and stay loose, and trusted the defense to close it out. He praised Deshaun Watson for playing well in the second half, especially with his legs, and said he did it without much of a run game, which Monken took responsibility for fixing schematically and with his play calling. Asked directly whether Watson starts at home against Carolina, Monken avoided answering and only said he was happy for him. He blamed the sloppy first half on Tampa's pressure from Todd Bowles, lost-yardage plays, holding penalties and failed conversions, and said the offense got the ball out quickly because there was no run game. On Denzel Boston, he said the team simply needed to get him the ball more. He credited the defense and coordinator Rudy for bouncing back and said the team will now prepare for Carolina.

signals.claim: Watson's status as starting QB against Carolina was not confirmed.
signals.note: Monken praised Watson but refused to commit to him as the Week 3 starter, so his job security is still an open question.

signals.claim: Watson will keep using his legs and distributing the ball quickly against pressure.
signals.note: His rushing contributions and quick passing helped the offense function without a run game, which boosts his fantasy floor.
signals.quote: he made some really nice plays with his legs, man.

signals.claim: Boston should get more targets going forward.
signals.note: Monken said the offense needed to get Boston the ball more, which points to a larger target share.
signals.quote: Other than we needed him to get the ball more.

signals.note: Fannin was the target on a key third-and-one conversion that extended a drive, which shows he is a trusted option in short-yardage situations.
signals.quote: the first third and one that he got it to Harold that extended the drive.

topics.detail: Monken admitted the Browns ran the ball poorly and could not control the line of scrimmage. He took responsibility for fixing it through scheme and play calling, so expect an emphasis on the ground game against Carolina.

Tampa's pressure from Todd Bowles, along with lost-yardage plays, holding penalties and missed conversions, led to a sloppy first half. The offense responded with quick throws to get the ball out of Watson's hands.
Monken credited the defense and coordinator Rudy for bouncing back after Week 1 and closing out the win after the delay.
The roughly two-hour delay was used to hydrate, fuel and keep the players loose, and the coaches prepared the skill players for chunk-play and two-minute situations.

title: Matt LaFleur: "I can't give enough credit to our defense"
headline: Jayden Reed has movement in all extremities but stays overnight after being carted off, and the O-line is badly depleted (Zach Tom 'out a long time', Monk and Banks in question) heading into a short week.
summary: LaFleur opened with injury news. Jayden Reed has movement in all his extremities and will stay in the hospital overnight after being carted off, which LaFleur called very scary. A second player, captioned as 'Zach Thomas' and almost certainly Zach Tom, doesn't look good and could be out a long time. He praised the team's resilience in coming back from 10 down in the fourth quarter to win in overtime, crediting the defense (pressure, run defense, an aggressive Jonathan Gannon game plan) and special teams for flipping the field. The offense was inconsistent, with too many negative plays and penalties (14 on the day, 26 in two games), and he said it must improve quickly on a short week. The line was so thin that the team was down to four linemen at one point and discussed putting Tucker Kraft at tackle while Jacob Monk was evaluated. He praised Jager Burton and Anthony Belton for stepping in and refused to discuss a trade for line help. He said Lukas Van Ness is coming into his own and that Kaleb Johnson was a good outside-zone runner who should earn more opportunities. He also noted that all three backs contributed, including Chris Brooks on a checkdown. He called Jordan Love a 'stud' with elite poise.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Vikings Win Over Bears, Dallas Turner’s Big Game & Battling Weather Conditions
headline: Vikings beat the Bears to go 2-0 in a sloppy, weather-hit game. Aaron Jones was the lone back, Dallas Turner dominated, Kyler Murray is expected to clear the concussion protocol early next week, and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (hip) is a question mark.
summary: O'Connell praised the team for winning a sloppy, weather-affected game at Soldier Field with no turnovers, two takeaways and very few penalties. He credited the defense for keeping the Bears out of the end zone, which let the offense run the football and play a clock-and-possession game. Aaron Jones was essentially the only running back and held up under a heavy workload, and O'Connell praised his vision and toughness. Carson Wentz made a big third-down conversion on the final clock-killing drive. Kyler Murray left the game early (the coach referred to him going down around the 10th or 11th play), but O'Connell said nothing has changed, Murray is feeling well, and he expects him to clear the protocol early in the week. O'Connell singled out Dallas Turner's dominant game and rapid growth. T.J. Hockenson, Justin Jefferson and Josh Oliver were credited with key catches, and the offensive line was praised for leaning on the run in poor conditions. Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins left with a right hip injury and did not return, and the team will evaluate him. O'Connell also said the offense was playing short-handed and that some players stepped into bigger roles.

injuries.detail: Right hip injury; did not return to the game. The team will evaluate him and provide an update.
Left the game early and is in the concussion protocol. O'Connell said nothing has changed, he is feeling well, and he expects him to clear the protocol early in the week.

signals.claim: Dallas Turner's growth has made him a central, dominant piece of the pass rush and defense.
signals.note: O'Connell called him the closer, which is a strong IDP/edge signal.
signals.quote: And his ascension is, you know, as as expected as it is

signals.note: He is on track to be back for the next game, but the protocol needs to be cleared.

signals.note: He is the backup if Murray's protocol drags on, though Murray is expected back.
signals.quote: Carson making a big third down conversion

signals.note: He is a reliable target even in a run-heavy, bad-weather game.

topics.detail: The team practiced Friday in similar wet conditions in the Twin Cities, working on footing, ball security and pitch-and-catch. The plan was to run the ball, limit turnovers and win with defense and special teams.

O'Connell loved the game plan from coordinator Flo and his staff: sound tackling, setting edges and funneling the ball. They kept Caleb Williams contained, and the back end plastered receivers. Late stops included a blocked field goal and Jalen Redmond's punch-out, recovered by a teammate, and Isaiah Rodgers had a late interception.
O'Connell said he saw progress from Caleb Banks, who had about six tackles and made some huge snaps. He said he is gaining confidence.
At 2-0 after opening against the Packers and Bears, O'Connell said the team is still learning but has a good defense and an offense that protects the football. He expects more adversity ahead.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 9/20: "I'm proud of our defense, I'm proud of everybody"
headline: Patriots beat Pittsburgh behind a harassing defense despite a rash of injuries; offense scored only 13 and Vrabel defended Drake Maye, while Romeo Doubs bounced back with two explosive plays.
summary: Vrabel praised the defense for a second straight strong game, saying affecting the quarterback every week is the formula. He said the team played a lot of newly arrived players because of injuries and that they were ready, but the team has to get healthy and see who is available next week for a big challenge. He gave no injury updates. He credited Christian Barmore for a holding penalty and forced fumble, and Elijah Ponder for scoring on a fumble recovery. He praised edge rushers Gabe Jacas and Ponder as the guys who have been playing, and described Jacas as a hard worker who learns through his mistakes. On offense, he said the unit executed well on TreVeyon Henderson's touchdown but did not finish enough drives. He deflected a question about whether Maye is pressing, said he will trust his decisions, and said he would review the tape on Maye's interception. He defended Romeo Doubs after a one-drop first week and said the receiver worked hard and got good opportunities from Maye. He also said Christian Gonzalez shadowed Metcalf and wants those challenges.

injuries.detail: Vrabel said the team had a lot of injuries during the game, gave no update on anyone, and said the team needs to get healthy and see who is available next week.

signals.note: Doubs bounced back from a drop last week with two explosive plays and the coach defended him, which supports his WR role.

signals.claim: The offense needs to finish more drives and Maye must make better decisions; the coach will review the interception on tape.
signals.note: The offense has scored only 13 and 10 points in two games, and Maye took sacks and threw an interception, so his production is worth monitoring.
signals.quote: I'm always going to trust his decision.

signals.note: Henderson scored a first-quarter touchdown that Vrabel highlighted as a key play.

He said the defense has to affect the quarterback each week, and that coverage must hold long enough for the rush to arrive.

title: Kellen Moore reacts to Saints' Win against Ravens | Saints-Ravens Postgame | 2026 NFL Week 2
headline: Saints beat Ravens as Tyler Shough and Juwan Johnson come up big late; Kelvin Banks has an ankle injury, and Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson saw reduced roles.
summary: Moore praised the team's resiliency in a Week 2 road win over Baltimore. The offense kicked field goals for much of the game and was stuck behind the sticks with penalties and long-yardage downs. A big drive after a three-and-out got it going, and Juwan Johnson's catch and run on third-and-8 set up the late touchdown. Moore called Tyler Shough steady and unflinching under exotic pressure, and said he converted key third downs. The goal-line sneaks on third and fourth down failed, and a false start pushed the offense back to the 7. The defense limited Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry in the second half through line, edge and blitzing linebacker pressure, and Moore singled out a rush on the late interception. Kelvin Banks left with an ankle injury that will be evaluated Monday, and a backup lineman stepped in well. Travis Etienne saw more work in the second half, which Moore called game flow. On inactives, he cited numbers: Johnson was sick during the week, Oscar Delp was coming back, and Chase Young and Cam Jordan were returning. He said Donaldson's fullback package was used less than normal and that Kendre Miller will still play plenty.

injuries.detail: Ankle injury suffered in the game; Moore said they will see how it looks tomorrow.

signals.claim: Shough remains the starting QB and is trusted in high-pressure, late-game situations.
signals.note: Moore praised his steadiness, third-down execution and toughness against pressure, which supports his fantasy floor.
signals.quote: the game's not too big for him ever.

title: Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (9/20) | Week 2
headline: Mason Taylor (thumb) and David Onyemata (groin) are banged up and updates are due this week; the Jets' run game never got going in a Week 2 overtime loss.
summary: Aaron Glenn was highly upset after a tough overtime loss and said it does not define the team. He listed several injuries and promised updates later in the week. He blamed penalties (13 for the Jets, 14 for the opponent), poor special teams, and never establishing the run. He also said the defense let the opponent move the ball and recovered only one of many forced fumbles. He defended taking the ball first in overtime, arguing that a long, clock-eating drive that ends in a score puts pressure on the other team, and pointed to the 19-play drive against Tennessee. He also defended going for it on fourth down at midfield and running the ball. He said he still trusts the run game, but would have to check the tape on why it failed against a strong interior and edge-setting defensive line. The first three overtime plays were dropbacks, and Geno Smith was sacked twice. Glenn said he trusts Geno and the offensive staff but called Geno's day 'probably not his best.' He said Jarvis Brownlee's emotional penalty can't happen. He also said he never considered a timeout late in regulation. Next up is a road game against an opponent he knows very well.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: September 20, 2026
headline: Eagles won 24-20 but lost Saquon Barkley, Dallas Goedert and Landon Dickerson during the game, and Sirianni gave no injury updates. The run game still needs work, and the line was reshuffled with Drew Kendall apparently at center.
summary: Sirianni called the 24-20 win over the Titans an organizational win. He credited attention to detail across the building, especially with how hot it was (he needed an IV after the game). He praised Jalen Hurts for shaking off a Jeffrey Simmons-forced interception and leading a quick game-winning drive that scored with about nine seconds left. He said the explosive plays, Sean's play-calling, Hurts' throws, DeVonta Smith's plays and strong pass protection made that drive work. On the injuries, Barkley and Goedert were raised by reporters and Sirianni himself mentioned Dickerson going out. He gave no details on any of them and credited the backups and the front office for the depth. He moved the offensive line around, with a natural center (apparently Drew Kendall) in the middle and Cam shifting to left guard. He called it the best lineup for this game and said "we'll see" about keeping it going forward. He hadn't seen the rushing numbers but said the team wants to run more efficiently, and he admitted there is room for improvement. He singled out Darius Cooper as a role player who did the dirty work, made nice plays and a special-teams tackle, and said the team will keep needing him in that role. The team has Monday off and returns to work Tuesday.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the loss to the Patriots
headline: McCarthy owns a flat 20-3 offensive showing, says he'll cut the play-call volume, and signals more opportunities for Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson with Michael Pittman banged up; Rico Dowdle's injury status is unknown.
summary: McCarthy took blame for the offense after the 20-3 loss to New England, saying the detail wasn't there and that he felt it in practice on Wednesday and Thursday. He said protections were not clean, communication broke down in the first half, and the Patriots' pressure plus man-to-man coverage on routes cost the offense big-play chances. The run game was 'herky jerky' and the trench play needs to improve. His main fix is cutting the offensive volume, citing Marty Schottenheimer's lesson that you reduce volume when you're not clean. He said Aaron Rodgers can handle any volume, but the team must give him better platforms to throw from, and he still wants to push the ball downfield. He called the defense good enough to win, holding New England to 13 points, and said special teams were a wash pending film review. On personnel, he said it's only two weeks in and didn't commit to changes, but said Michael Pittman has been fighting through injuries and that it creates opportunities for others, naming Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson. He had no update on Rico Dowdle's injury and confirmed Rodgers' exit was situational.

title: Todd Bowles on Result of Browns vs. Bucs | Press Conference
headline: Bowles blamed penalties and missed tackles for the Week 2 loss to Cleveland, said Godwin and Egbuka were doubled in the first half, and promised a better early ground game and quicker passes.
summary: Bowles opened by saying the Bucs were undone by too many offensive penalties and too many missed tackles in the second half, and that the team has to fix itself quickly because nobody is coming to save them. He called the 0-2 start an adverse situation and said the team has handled adversity before. On offense, he defended throwing in the rain on early downs as a way to factor in the clock and keep the Browns from being easy to play against, and he admitted the passes didn't work. He said the team needs a better ground game early and more quick passes. Asked why Chris Godwin and Emeka Egbuka were barely involved in the first half, he said Cleveland took them away and doubled them a few times, but he wants to watch the film before saying for sure. He said the heavy use of screens to the running backs was something the Browns' coverage gave them on tape. On defense, he blamed missed tackles for Deshaun Watson and the Browns' second-half run, including a collision between two Bucs defenders that led to a touchdown run. He thought the pass rush was better than the previous week, though Watson's mobility and elusiveness in the pocket hurt it. He also said the long weather delay was no excuse, since both teams dealt with it.

signals.note: The quiet first half looks coverage-driven rather than a role change, so a rebound is plausible, but Bowles hasn't confirmed it.
signals.quote: I know they doubled them a few times.

signals.claim: Egbuka was doubled at times in the first half, and Bowles will review the film to confirm why he was barely involved.

topics.detail: Bowles named offensive penalties and second-half missed tackles as the main problems. He said the team must correct both quickly.

He said the Bucs need a better ground game early and more quick passes. The early-down passes in the rain were meant to factor in the clock and didn't work. The screen-heavy approach was what Cleveland's defense gave them on tape.

Watson's second-half success came from missed tackles, including two Bucs colliding and missing on a touchdown run. Bowles said the pass rush improved over the previous week but was hampered by Watson's mobility.
Bowles said the multi-hour weather delay was no excuse because both teams dealt with it. He framed the 0-2 start as adversity the team must overcome.
